newsitem.title: UK: U.S. approves Glaxo 311C90 sale to Zeneca.
newsitem.headline: U.S. approves Glaxo 311C90 sale to Zeneca.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said it had gained U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) approval for the sale of the anti-migraine compound 311C90 to Zeneca.
Glaxo said it had to sell the compound as a condition of its acquisition of Wellcome last year.
The consideration for the sale comprises initial and milestone payments which are not material to Glaxo Wellcome or Zeneca, the statement said.
The companies said that certain further payments might be due, depending on the level of sales.
Zeneca and Glaxo expect to close the deal in the next few days.
The compound is a 5-HT1D agonist in Phase III development for the treatment of migraine.
"311C90 offers additional exciting growth prospects for us in the primary care market," said Tom McKillop, chief executive officer of Zeneca Pharmaceuticals.
"Zeneca has now assumed responsibility for development and our aim is an early regulatory submission and launch," he added.
The compound will be marketed under the name "Zomig" in most countries, Zeneca said.
The worldwide migraine treatment market is expected to reach 1.5 billion stg by the year 2000.
